entities.name: Lucius Marcius Censorinus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lucius Marcius Censorinus was a Roman politician and military leader of the Middle Republic, serving as consul with Manius Manilius in 149 BC and censor in 147 BC. He led the fleet during the first phase of the Third Punic War.

As a prominent figure of the Roman Republic, Censorinus played a crucial role in shaping the politics and military strategies of the time. His leadership during the Third Punic War had significant implications for the fate of Carthage and the Mediterranean region.

Censorinus's legacy can be seen in the Roman law codes that were established during his tenure as censor. The Twelve Tables, a foundational document of Roman law, were largely compiled during his time in office. These laws had a lasting impact on the development of Western jurisprudence.

The Roman historian Suetonius famously declared that Censorinus was 'a man of great dignity and noble birth,' whose reputation was 'not less esteemed by the Roman people than that of the most illustrious of their consuls.' This assessment reflects the high esteem in which Censorinus was held by his contemporaries.

Despite the significance of his achievements, Censorinus's personal life remains somewhat of a mystery. The exact date of his birth and death are unknown, adding to the enigma surrounding his life.
